questions.question: Which of the following is formed by a chemical reaction?
questions.solution:

• **Water** is a chemical **compound** consisting of two **hydrogen** atoms and one **oxygen** atom, represented by the chemical formula **H2O**.
 
• It is formed through a **chemical reaction** (such as the combustion of hydrogen in the presence of oxygen) where the constituent elements undergo a transformation to form a new substance with entirely different properties. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• During the formation of water, **chemical bonds** (specifically **polar covalent bonds**) are created between the atoms. This process usually involves the release of energy, making it an **exothermic reaction**.
 
• Compounds like water have a **fixed composition** by mass. In water, **hydrogen** and **oxygen** always combine in a fixed ratio of **1:8** by **mass**, regardless of the source.
 
• Unlike mixtures, the components of a compound like **water** cannot be separated by simple **physical methods** like filtration or evaporation; they require **chemical methods** like **electrolysis** to break back down into elements.

questions.question: An athlete runs around a circular track with radius r , completing one full round in t seconds. Which of the following correctly represents the athlete's speed v ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**v = 2π r / t**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **speed** of an object is defined as the **total distance** traveled divided by the **total time** taken to cover that distance.
 
• In this scenario, the athlete is running on a **circular track**. The distance covered in **one full round** is equal to the **circumference** of the circle.
 
• The mathematical formula for the **circumference** of a circle with **radius r** is given by **2πr**.
 
• The **time** taken to complete one full round is provided as **t seconds**.
 
• By applying the basic formula for **average speed** (Speed = Distance / Time), we substitute the distance with **2πr** and the time with **t**.
 
• Therefore, the correct expression for the **athlete's speed v** is **v = 2π r / t**. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***

questions.question: If the distance (d) between the Earth and the Moon decreases gradually, then what will happen to the gravitational force (F) between them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between the gravitational force and the distance between two celestial bodies is governed by **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**.
 
• The law states that the **gravitational force (F)** between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses and **inversely proportional to the square of the distance (d)** between their centers.
 
• Mathematically, the formula is expressed as **F = G × (m1 × m2) / d²**, where **G** is the universal gravitational constant, **m1** is the mass of the **Earth**, and **m2** is the mass of the **Moon**.
 
• Because the distance **(d)** is in the denominator as a squared term, even a small decrease in distance leads to a significant increase in the force of attraction. This is known as the **Inverse Square Law**.
 
• If the distance **(d)** between the Earth and the Moon decreases gradually, the value of **1/d²** increases, which directly causes the **gravitational force (F)** to **increase**. ***Hence, the correct option is Increases.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G):** This is a physical constant involved in the calculation of gravitational effects. Its value is approximately **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²**. It remains constant throughout the universe regardless of the environment or the nature of the bodies.
 
• **Mass of the Earth and Moon:** The **Earth** has a mass of approximately **5.972 × 10²⁴ kg**, while the **Moon** has a mass of about **7.347 × 10²² kg**. Because both masses are very large, the resulting gravitational force is powerful enough to maintain the Moon's **orbital velocity**.
 
• **Nature of Gravitational Force:** It is a **conservative force**, meaning the work done by gravity on an object is independent of the path taken. It is also a **central force**, acting along the line joining the centers of the two masses.
 
• **Vector Quantity:** Gravitational force is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. The direction is always attractive, pulling the Moon toward the center of the Earth and vice versa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tidal Effects:** The gravitational pull of the Moon is the primary cause of **ocean tides** on Earth. If the distance decreased, the **tidal force** (which is proportional to **1/d³**) would increase even more rapidly than the gravitational force, leading to much more extreme high and low tides.
 
• **Roche Limit:** If the Moon were to decrease its distance significantly and cross a specific threshold called the **Roche Limit** (approximately **9,500 km** to **18,000 km** from Earth depending on composition), the **tidal forces** would overcome the Moon's own gravity, causing it to break apart and potentially form a **ring system** around Earth.
 
• **Current Reality:** In reality, the Moon is not moving closer; it is actually **receding** from the Earth at a rate of approximately **3.8 centimeters** per **year** due to tidal acceleration and the transfer of **angular momentum**.
 
• **Barycenter:** The Earth and Moon actually orbit around a common center of mass called the **Barycenter**. As the distance decreases, the location of this Barycenter would shift closer to the center of the Earth, altering the Earth's "wobble" in space.

questions.question: Power measures:

options.text: how fast or slow work is done
the energy stored in an object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**how fast or slow work is done**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the **rate of doing work** or the **rate of transferring energy**. It determines how quickly a particular task is completed. ***Hence, the correct answer is how fast or slow work is done.***
 
• In physical terms, if an agent does a certain amount of **Work (W)** in a **Time interval (t)**, then the **Average Power** is calculated as the ratio of work to time. The mathematical expression is **Power = Work / Time**.
 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, which is equivalent to **one Joule per second (1 J/s)**. This unit was named in honor of **James Watt**, the **18th-century** developer of the steam engine.
 
• Because power only has magnitude and no specific direction, it is classified as a **Scalar quantity**.
 
• The concept of power is essential in evaluating the efficiency of **engines**, **motors**, and **electrical appliances**, where the speed of energy consumption or output is more critical than the total energy used.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Units of Power:**
 
 
• Beyond the Watt, other common units include the **Kilowatt (kW)**, which equals **1,000 Watts**, and the **Megawatt (MW)**, which equals **1,000,000 Watts**.
 
• In the automotive and industrial sectors, **Horsepower (hp)** is frequently used. One standard unit of **Horsepower** is approximately equal to **746 Watts**.
 
 
 
• **Power vs. Energy:**
 
 
• While **Energy** is the capacity to do work (measured in **Joules**), **Power** is the speed at which that energy is used. For example, two people might climb the same flight of stairs (doing the same work), but the one who runs up faster generates more **Power**.
 
• The **total work done** refers to the total energy expended and does not account for the time duration, which distinguishes it from power.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Power:**
 
 
• In electrical circuits, power is the product of **Voltage (V)** and **Current (I)**. The formula is **P = V x I**. This is crucial for determining the **electricity consumption** of household devices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional representation of power is **[ML²T^-3]**. This is derived from the dimensions of work **[ML²T^-2]** divided by the dimension of time **[T]**.
 
• **Instantaneous Power:** This refers to the power at a specific moment in time. It can be calculated as the **dot product** of **Force (F)** and **Velocity (v)**, expressed as **P = F . v**.
 
• **Commercial Unit of Energy:** It is important to distinguish power from the **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**. Although it contains the word "watt," the **kWh** is actually a unit of **Energy** (Power multiplied by Time), used by utility companies to bill for electricity usage. **1 kWh** is equal to **3.6 million Joules**.
 
• **Energy Stored:** The **energy stored in an object** (like potential or kinetic energy) is a measure of its **capacity** to do work, not the rate at which it is done. Similarly, the **height of an object** is a spatial dimension that influences **Potential Energy** but does not measure power directly.
</ul

questions.question: In plants, asexual reproduction involves ________.

options.text: fusion of male and female gametes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**only one parent organism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** is a mode of reproduction that does not involve the **fusion of gametes** or change in the number of **chromosomes**.
 
• In plants, **asexual reproduction** involves **only one parent organism** to produce offspring. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• The process of **sexual reproduction** requires **both parent organisms** (male and female) to contribute genetic material. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• The **fusion of male and female gametes** is a primary characteristic of **sexual reproduction**, which leads to genetic variation. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Fusion and fertilisation** are steps specifically associated with sexual cycles to form a **zygote**; these do not occur in asexual methods. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The resulting offspring in asexual reproduction are **genetically identical** to the parent, often referred to as **clones**, as they are produced through **mitotic divisions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• This is a common form of **asexual reproduction** in plants where new plants are produced from **roots, stems, leaves, and buds**.
 
• **Stem:** Examples include **Potato** (tubers with eyes), **Ginger** (rhizomes), and **Sugar cane**.
 
• **Roots:** Plants like **Sweet potato** and **Dahlia** can give rise to new plants from their adventitious roots.
 
• **Leaves:** The **Bryophyllum** (sprout leaf plant) has buds in the margins of its leaves that can grow into new plants when they fall on moist soil.
 
 
 
• **Budding:**
 
 
• Commonly observed in **Yeast**, where a small bulb-like projection called a **bud** grows out from the parent body, matures, and eventually detaches to form a new individual.
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation:**
 
 
• In certain **Algae** like **Spirogyra**, the plant body breaks into two or more **fragments**, and each piece grows into a complete new organism.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation:**
 
 
• Plants like **Ferns and Mosses** reproduce through **spores**. These are asexual bodies covered by a hard **protective coat** to survive unfavorable conditions like high temperature and low humidity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Reproduction Modes:**
 
 
• **Asexual Reproduction**: Only **one parent** is involved, no **seeds** are produced, and it occurs in a **short period** of time.
 
• **Sexual Reproduction**: **Two parents** are involved, **seeds** are produced through the **pollination** and **fertilization** process, and it takes a **longer time** to complete.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Asexual Reproduction:**
 
 
• Plants produced this way reach **maturity** faster and bear **flowers and fruits** earlier than those produced from seeds.
 
• It is an **economical** and quick method for **multiplication**, especially in agriculture and horticulture (e.g., **grafting, layering**).
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages:**
 
 
• Since there is no **genetic recombination**, the offspring lack **diversity**, making them highly susceptible to the same **diseases** or environmental changes.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The distance between the pole and the centre of curvature of a concave mirror is – 50 cm. If the magnification produced is (–1) by this mirror, then what will be the object and the image distance, respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**- 50 cm and - 50 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The distance between the **pole (P)** and the **centre of curvature (C)** of a spherical mirror is known as the **Radius of Curvature (R)**. For the given **concave mirror**, this distance is **- 50 cm**.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the distance of the object and image are measured from the pole. Since the centre of curvature of a **concave mirror** lies in front of the reflecting surface, **R** is taken as **negative**.
 
• The **Magnification (m)** produced by a mirror is the ratio of the image distance to the object distance with a negative sign, expressed as **m = -v/u**. Given **m = - 1**, it implies that **- 1 = -v/u**, which simplifies to **v = u**.
 
• A **magnification** of **- 1** specifically indicates that the image is **real, inverted**, and the **same size** as the object. This specific condition occurs in a **concave mirror** only when the object is placed exactly at the **Centre of Curvature (C)**.

questions.question: In a v–t graph, if the slope keeps changing, it means:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**acceleration is non-uniform**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **v–t graph** (Velocity-Time graph), the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration** of the moving object.
 
• If the **slope keeps changing** at different points on the graph, it indicates that the **rate of change of velocity** is not constant over **time**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Uniform acceleration** is represented by a **straight line** with a **constant slope**, meaning the **velocity** increases or decreases by equal amounts in equal intervals of **time**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• If the **speed is constant**, the **velocity** does not change, resulting in a **slope of zero**. This is represented by a **horizontal straight line** parallel to the **time axis**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The **displacement** of an object is calculated by the **area under the curve** of a **v–t graph**. A changing slope describes how the **velocity** is changing, but it does not imply that the **displacement** is **zero**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is acceleration is non-uniform.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• It is a **vector quantity** defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **acceleration** is **m/s²** (meters per second squared).
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration** occurs when an object's **velocity** changes by **unequal amounts** in **equal intervals of time**, resulting in a **curved line** on a **v–t graph**.
 
 
 
• **Graph Interpretations:**
 
 
• In a **Distance-Time graph**, the **slope** represents **speed**.
 
• In a **Displacement-Time graph**, the **slope** represents **velocity**.
 
• In a **Velocity-Time graph**, a **positive slope** indicates **acceleration**, while a **negative slope** indicates **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• For **uniform acceleration**, the three **kinematic equations** used are **v = u + at**, **s = ut + 1/2at²**, and **v² = u² + 2as**, where **u** is **initial velocity** and **v** is **final velocity**.
 
• These equations cannot be directly applied to **non-uniform acceleration**; instead, **calculus** (differentiation and integration) is required.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Instantaneous Acceleration:** When the **slope** of a **v–t graph** is **changing**, the **acceleration** at any **specific second** is called **instantaneous acceleration**, which is the **slope of the tangent** at that point.
 
• **Zero Acceleration:** This occurs when an object moves with **constant velocity**. The **v–t graph** is a **flat line**, and the **slope** is **0**.
 
• **Area Calculation:** To find the **total distance** traveled from a **v–t graph**, one must calculate the **magnitude** of the **area** between the curve and the **time axis**.
 
• **Real-world Examples:** A **car driving through heavy traffic** or a **bus stopping at intervals** are classic examples of **non-uniform acceleration**, where the **v–t graph** would show a **continuously changing slope**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct?

options.text: The SI unit of power of lens is Dioptre (D).
A 5D lens has focal length 20 m.
A 2D lens has focal length 0.5 m.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A 5D lens has focal length 20 m.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **power of a lens** is defined as the ability of a lens to converge or diverge light rays. Mathematically, it is the **reciprocal of its focal length** (f) in meters.
 
• The **SI unit** of power of a lens is **Dioptre**, which is denoted by the symbol **D**. If the focal length is expressed in **meters (m)**, then power is expressed in **dioptres**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• For a lens with a power of **5D**, the focal length (f) can be calculated using the formula **f = 1/P**. Here, **f = 1/5 = 0.2 meters**. Since **0.2 meters** is equal to **20 centimeters (cm)**, the claim that it has a focal length of **20 m** is mathematically incorrect. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• By definition, **1 Dioptre** is the power of a lens whose **focal length** is exactly **1 meter** (1 D = 1 m⁻¹). This serves as the standard unit for ophthalmic prescriptions. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• For a lens with a power of **2D**, the focal length is calculated as **f = 1/P = 1/2 = 0.5 meters**. This is a consistent application of the lens power formula. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the incorrect statement (and the correct answer) is "A 5D lens has focal length 20 m."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Lenses and Sign Convention**:
 
 
• A **Convex lens** (converging lens) has a **positive focal length**; therefore, its **power is always positive**.
 
• A **Concave lens** (diverging lens) has a **negative focal length**; therefore, its **power is always negative**.
 
• When an optician prescribes a **corrective lens** with a power of +2.0 D, it means the person requires a convex lens. Conversely, a power of -2.0 D indicates a requirement for a concave lens.
 
 
 
• **Combination of Lenses**:
 
 
• When multiple thin lenses are placed in **contact** with each other, the **total power (P)** of the combination is the **algebraic sum** of the individual powers of the lenses.
 
• Formula: **P = P1 + P2 + P3 + ...**
 
• This principle is widely used in designing **camera lenses**, **microscopes**, and **telescopes** to minimize aberrations and improve image quality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Focal Length Conversion**: While calculating power, it is vital to ensure the focal length is in **meters**. If the focal length is given in **centimeters (cm)**, the formula used is **P = 100/f (in cm)**.
 
• **Lensmeter**: The professional instrument used by optometrists and opticians to verify the **correct power** of a spectacle lens is known as a **Lensmeter** or **Focimeter**.
 
• **Human Eye Power**: The **cornea** and **crystalline lens** of the human eye provide a combined power of approximately **60 dioptres** when the eye is at rest, focusing on distant objects.
 
• **Magnification**: While power relates to the bending of light, **magnification** refers to the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object. They are related but distinct concepts in **optics**.

questions.question: What will happen if the dendrites of neurons do not function?

options.text: Neurons will produce more electrical impulses
Signals from other neurons will not be received

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Signals from other neurons will not be received**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dendrites** are the **projections** of a **neuron** (nerve cell) that receive signals (information) from other neurons. They act like the "antennae" of the cell, and their primary **function** is to pick up **chemical signals** called **neurotransmitters**.
 
• If the **dendrites** do not function, the neuron will lose its ability to detect incoming stimuli from the **synapse** (the gap between neurons). Consequently, the **Signals from other neurons will not be received**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• A neuron produces **electrical impulses** (action potentials) only after it has processed incoming signals received through its dendrites. If these inputs are blocked, the frequency of impulses would likely drop to zero rather than increasing. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Muscle contraction** occurs when **motor neurons** send signals to **muscle fibers**.

questions.question: What is the name of the long, fibre-like part of a neuron that carries signals away from the cell body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Axon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neuron** is the basic functional unit of the **nervous system**, designed to transmit information to other nerve cells, muscle, or gland cells.
 
• The **Axon** is a long, slender, tube-like projection of a nerve cell that conducts electrical impulses, known as **action potentials**, away from the **cell body** (soma).
 
• While a neuron may have many dendrites, it typically has only **one axon**, which can range in length from a fraction of a **millimeter** to over **1 meter** in humans.
 
• The primary function of the axon is to transmit information to different neurons, muscles, and glands; it acts as the primary "output" cable of the cell.
 
• The **axon hillock** is the specialized part of the cell body where the axon begins and where the summation of signals occurs before an impulse is fired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dendrites:**
 
 
• These are short, branched extensions of a neuron that receive signals from other neurons and carry them **toward** the cell body.
 
• They serve as the "input" sensors of the neuron, increasing the surface area available to receive **neurotransmitters**.
 
 
 
• **Synapse:**
 
 
• The **synapse** is the microscopic junction or gap between the **axon terminal** of one neuron and the dendrite or cell body of another.
 
• Information is transmitted across this gap through **chemical signaling** using molecules called **neurotransmitters**.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:**
 
 
• Found within the **soma** (cell body), the **nucleus** contains the genetic material (**DNA**) and coordinates the cell's activities like growth and reproduction.
 
• It is essential for the metabolic maintenance and protein synthesis required for the neuron's survival.
 
 
 
• **Soma (Cell Body):**
 
 
• This is the core part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and other organelles like **mitochondria** and **ribosomes**.
 
• It integrates incoming signals from the dendrites and maintains the life of the nerve cell.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Myelin Sheath:** Many axons are covered with a fatty insulating layer called the **myelin sheath**, produced by **Schwann cells** in the peripheral nervous system or **oligodendrocytes** in the central nervous system.
 
• **Nodes of Ranvier:** These are periodic gaps in the **myelin sheath** where the axon membrane is exposed; they facilitate the rapid "jumping" of impulses, a process called **saltatory conduction**.
 
• **Axon Terminals:** At its end, an axon branches into several **terminals** (telodendria), which contain **synaptic vesicles** that store and release chemicals to communicate with the next cell.
 
• **Direction of Flow:** In a typical neuron, the flow of information is **unidirectional**: Dendrites → Cell Body → Axon → Axon Terminals.
</ul

questions.question: A stethoscope helps a doctor hear a patient’s heartbeat clearly. Which principle does a stethoscope use for this purpose?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Multiple reflection of sound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **stethoscope** is a vital medical instrument used by doctors to listen to sounds produced within the body, primarily the **heartbeat** and **lung sounds**.
 
• The basic principle behind the functioning of a stethoscope is the **multiple reflection of sound**. Sound waves originating from the patient's body travel through the air-filled tube of the stethoscope.
 
• As the sound waves move through the tube, they undergo **successive reflections** from the inner walls of the tubing. This ensures that the sound energy remains confined within the tube and is directed toward the doctor's ears without significant loss of intensity. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The instrument consists of a **chest piece**, which typically has a **diaphragm** (for high-frequency sounds) and a **bell** (for low-frequency sounds), connected to **binaural earpieces** by flexible **tubing**.
 
• When the **heart beats**, it creates pressure waves. The **diaphragm** of the stethoscope vibrates due to these waves, and these vibrations are converted into sound waves that undergo **multiple reflections** to reach the observer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Interference of Sound**:
 
 
• **Interference** is the phenomenon that occurs when two or more sound waves overlap to form a resultant wave of greater, lower, or the same amplitude.
 
• While interference is a fundamental property of waves, it is not the primary mechanism used in a standard stethoscope to transmit heartbeat sounds. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Refraction of Sound**:
 
 
• **Refraction** involves the bending of sound waves as they pass from one medium to another or through a medium with varying properties like **temperature** or **density**.
 
• For instance, sound travels faster in **warm air** than in **cold air**, causing it to bend. This principle is not utilized by a stethoscope to guide sound to the ears. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Diffraction of Sound**:
 
 
• **Diffraction** refers to the bending of waves around the corners of an obstacle or through an aperture.
 
• This explains why we can hear someone talking from around a corner, but it is not the method by which a stethoscope amplifies or clarifies internal body sounds. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The first stethoscope was invented by **René Laennec** in **1816** in **France**. It was a simple wooden tube used for **auscultation**.
 
• Before this invention, doctors practiced **immediate auscultation** by placing their ear directly on the patient's chest.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Laws of Reflection**: Sound follows the same laws of reflection as light. The **angle of incidence** is equal to the **angle of reflection**, and the incident wave, reflected wave, and the normal all lie in the same plane.
 
• **Applications of Multiple Reflection**:
 
 
• **Megaphones** and **horns** are designed to send sound in a particular direction by using **multiple reflections**.
 
• The ceilings of **concert halls** and **cinema halls** are often curved so that sound after reflection reaches all corners of the hall.
 
• **Soundboards** are sometimes placed behind speakers in large halls to reflect sound toward the audience.
 
 
 
• **Modern Stethoscopes**: Today, **electronic stethoscopes** are available that use **piezoelectric crystals** to convert sound vibrations into electrical signals, which are then amplified and processed for better clarity and noise reduction.

questions.question: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When resistors are connected in a **parallel combination**, the reciprocal of the **equivalent resistance (Rp)** is equal to the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
• The mathematical formula for three resistors in parallel is **1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3**. In this case, the values are **2 Ω**, **3 Ω**, and **6 Ω**.
 
• Applying the values: **1/Rp = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6**. To solve this, we find a common denominator, which is **6**. The calculation becomes **3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6**.
 
• Solving for **Rp**, we get **1/Rp = 1**, which means the **equivalent resistance** is **1 Ω**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 1 Ω.***
 
• A fundamental characteristic of **parallel circuits** is that the **total resistance** is always less than the value of the **smallest individual resistor** in the combination. Since **1 Ω** is less than **2 Ω**, the result is consistent with physical laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Series Combination:**
 
 
• In a **series circuit**, the total resistance is the algebraic sum of individual resistances: **Rs = R1 + R2 + R3**.
 
• If these three resistors (**2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω**) were connected in series, the equivalent resistance would be **11 Ω**.
 
• In series, the **current** remains constant through all components, but the **voltage** drops across each resistor.
 
 
 
• **Domestic Wiring Systems:**
 
 
• Most **household electrical appliances** are connected in **parallel**.
 
• This arrangement ensures that every appliance receives the same **voltage (220V in India)** and can be operated independently using separate switches.
 
• If one appliance fails or is turned off in a **parallel circuit**, the others continue to function normally.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Formulated by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the current (I) through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V) across it, provided physical conditions remain constant: **V = IR**.
 
• The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm**, symbolized by the Greek letter **Ω (Omega)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** The resistance of a conductor depends on its **length** (directly proportional), **area of cross-section** (inversely proportional), the **nature of the material** (resistivity), and **temperature**.
 
• **Conductance:** The reciprocal of resistance is called **conductance (G)**, measured in **Siemens (S)** or **mho**. In parallel circuits, the total conductance is simply the sum of individual conductances (**Gp = G1 + G2 + G3**).
 
• **Current Distribution:** In a **parallel combination**, the total current from the source is divided among the branches. The branch with the **lowest resistance** (the **2 Ω** resistor in this example) will carry the **highest current**.
 
• **Power Dissipation:** In parallel, the resistor with the **lowest resistance** dissipates the **most power** since Power **P = V² / R** and V is constant for all.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions DOES NOT support an increase in the rate of evaporation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An increase in humidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is a **surface phenomenon** in which molecules of a liquid undergo a phase transition into the **vapor state** at any temperature below its **boiling point**.
 
• **An increase of surface area**: Since evaporation happens at the surface, increasing the **exposed area** allows more molecules to escape into the air simultaneously, thereby **increasing** the rate of evaporation. *Hence, statement 1 supports an increase.*
 
• **An increase in wind speed**: Higher **wind speed** helps in moving the **water vapor particles** away from the liquid's surface, decreasing the concentration of vapor in the immediate vicinity and **accelerating** the process. *Hence, statement 2 supports an increase.*
 
• **An increase of temperature**: When the **temperature** rises, a greater number of particles gain enough **kinetic energy** to overcome the **intermolecular forces** of attraction and escape as vapor. *Hence, statement 3 supports an increase.*
 
• **An increase in humidity**: **Humidity** represents the amount of **water vapor** already present in the **atmosphere**. The air can only hold a **fixed amount** of moisture at a specific temperature; if the humidity is high, the air becomes **saturated**, which significantly **reduces** the rate of evaporation. *Hence, statement 4 does not support an increase and is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy and Evaporation**: Molecules in a liquid move at different **velocities**. Only those at the **surface** with high **kinetic energy** can break free from the liquid’s pull. As temperature increases, the **average kinetic energy** of the system rises, leading to faster evaporation.
 
• **Cooling Effect**: Evaporation causes a **cooling effect** because the escaping high-energy particles leave behind lower-energy particles, reducing the **overall temperature** of the liquid. This is the principle behind **sweating** in humans and the cooling of water in **earthen pots (matkas)**.
 
• **Nature of Liquid**: The rate also depends on the **intermolecular forces**. Liquids like **acetone**, **petrol**, or **perfume** have weak forces and evaporate much faster than water at **room temperature**.
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure**: A **decrease** in **atmospheric pressure** generally leads to an **increase** in the rate of evaporation, as there is less pressure exerted on the surface of the liquid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Boiling and Evaporation**: While **boiling** is a **bulk phenomenon** that occurs at a specific **boiling point** throughout the entire liquid, **evaporation** is a **surface phenomenon** that occurs at **all temperatures**.
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization**: During evaporation, the liquid absorbs **heat energy** (latent heat) from the surroundings or the body it is in contact with, which facilitates the **phase change** and results in **cooling**.
 
• **Practical Examples**:
 
 
• Spreading **wet clothes** on a **clothesline** increases the **surface area**, making them dry faster.
 
• In **coastal areas** where **humidity** is very high, clothes take a longer time to dry compared to **arid regions** or **deserts**.
 
• Using a **fan** increases the **wind speed**, which helps in drying **spilled water** on the floor quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions is essential for chlorine to react rapidly with an alkane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alkanes** are **saturated hydrocarbons** characterized by single bonds between carbon atoms. Due to their stable nature, they are often referred to as **paraffins**, meaning they have **little affinity** for chemical reagents under normal conditions.
 
• For **Chlorine** to react rapidly with an **alkane**, the presence of **Sunlight** (specifically **Ultraviolet (UV) radiation**) is essential to provide the necessary **activation energy**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Sunlight.***
 
• This specific type of reaction is known as a **Substitution Reaction** or **Photochemical Halogenation**. In this process, one or more **Hydrogen** atoms of the alkane are replaced by **Halogen** atoms.
 
• The **energy** from **Sunlight** causes the **homolytic fission** of the **Chlorine-Chlorine (Cl-Cl) bond**, leading to the formation of highly reactive **Chlorine Free Radicals**.
 
• **Presence of oxygen**: Oxygen can actually act as an **inhibitor** in free radical reactions because it reacts with radicals to form less reactive peroxy radicals, thereby slowing down the reaction. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **High pressure**: While pressure affects the rate of gaseous reactions, it is not the primary **trigger** or essential condition for the initiation of the alkane-chlorine substitution process. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **High temperature**: Although the reaction can occur at **high temperatures** (typically between **250 to 400 degrees Celsius**) in the dark, **Sunlight** is the most common and "essential" catalyst for the rapid reaction cited in standard organic chemistry. ***Hence, statement 4 is less appropriate compared to Sunlight in this context.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Free Radical Mechanism**: The reaction follows a three-step mechanism: **Initiation**, **Propagation**, and **Termination**.
 
 
• **Initiation**: The **UV light** breaks the **Cl2** molecule into two **Cl radicals**.
 
• **Propagation**: A **Chlorine radical** reacts with **Methane (CH4)** to form a **Methyl radical (CH3)** and **Hydrogen Chloride (HCl)**. The **Methyl radical** then reacts with another **Cl2** molecule to form **Chloromethane (CH3Cl)**.
 
• **Termination**: Two radicals combine to form a stable molecule, ending the **chain reaction**.
 
 
 
• **Chain Reaction**: Chlorination is a **chain reaction** because the **propagation** step regenerates a radical that continues the process until the reactants are consumed or radicals are destroyed.
 
• **Multiple Substitution**: If **Chlorine** is present in **excess**, the reaction continues until all **Hydrogen** atoms in the alkane are replaced, forming products like **Dichloromethane (CH2Cl2)**, **Chloroform (CHCl3)**, and **Carbon Tetrachloride (CCl4)**.
 
• **Reactivity of Halogens**: The rate of reaction with alkanes varies among halogens. **Fluorine** reacts explosively (most reactive), **Chlorine** and **Bromine** react at moderate rates under **Sunlight**, while **Iodine** reacts very slowly and the reaction is **reversible**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **diffused sunlight**, the reaction proceeds at a controlled rate to give a mixture of **alkyl halides**. However, in **direct sunlight**, the reaction can be **vigorous** or even **explosive**, sometimes resulting in the complete decomposition of the alkane into **Carbon** and **Hydrogen Chloride**.
 
• The necessity of **light** classifies this as a **Photochemical Reaction**. Without light or high heat, **Alkanes** and **Chlorine** can be stored together in the **dark** for long periods without any significant reaction.
 
• **Homolytic Fission**: This occurs when a covalent bond breaks such that each atom takes **one electron** from the shared pair, resulting in **neutral atoms** or groups with unpaired electrons called **Free Radicals**.
</ul
